findings.text: The sweep total is published as 184 and no subset of the record sums to it. The raw level table is 16+16+16+24+32+64 = 168; the figure's own eight rows (six levels plus the two c=32 repeats) sum to 232; performed-and-recorded including the rejected first c=64 attempt is 264. 184 matches none of them, and the figure's table and the '0 of 184' sentence were committed in the same commit describing the same sweep, so the two are read side by side. The figure is the one to trust: its per-row 'completed' column agrees with the raw file row for row. The manifest makes the contradiction internal to a single field, stating both '(n=16,16,16,24,32,64 requests)' and '184/184 completed'. This is the headline timeout figure of the done-when ('the timeout rate at concurrency 1, 4, 8, 16 and 32'), and the per-level timeout column does carry it correctly (0/16, 0/16, 0/16, 0/24, 0/32, 0/64) - it is only the aggregate that cannot be rederived. Fix: state 168 for the levels (or 232 including the repeats, or 264 including the rejected run) and say which set is meant. Propagation: the same 184 reached the plan comment, the commit body and a memory note, so it should be corrected at all four sites rather than only the visible one.

'The raw per-level and per-request values ship beside the figure' is asserted in the commit body, the evidence anchor and the manifest's artifacts field, and there is no per-request value anywhere in the file. What ships is six level rows, two repeat rows and one rejected row - aggregates only (p50/p95/max, n, wall, throughput, starvation count). The done-when asks for the per-level measurements, which ARE present and rederivable (I recomputed all six requests_per_min from n_requests/wall_s: 9.11, 21.32, 26.76, 29.74, 36.45, 34.30, every one matching), so the gate itself is met; the overstatement is in the surrounding prose. It matters because the level that carries the tail claim cannot be inspected: c=64 has lat_p95 null where every other level has one, while its lat_max is 111.93 s and 43 of its 64 requests exceeded the 60 s starvation deadline - so the column that would characterise the tail on the single level where the tail is the whole story is empty, and with no per-request values there is nothing to fall back on. Either ship the per-request array or drop the 'per-request' claim; if p95 is deliberately absent at c=64, say why.

The knee sentence mixes two bases for the c=32 level, and the direction word contradicts the arithmetic. The curve plots 36.45 as the c=32 point, but the '+1.5%' in the same sentence is 34.30 against the MEAN of the three c=32 samples (36.45+32.01+32.98)/3 = 33.81, i.e. +1.44%. Against the plotted 36.45 the c=64 reading is -5.9%. So the figure shows a falling curve and the caption describes a rise, and 'in the wrong direction' labels that rise a fall. The evidence anchor and the commit body repeat the same construction ('flattens at 64 (34.30, +1.5% inside a measured 13% run-to-run band)'). Rederiving from the raw file gives -5.9% on the plotted basis or +1.4% on the mean basis, never '+1.5% ... in the wrong direction'. The conclusion is not in danger - the mean basis (+1.4%) and the plotted basis (-5.9%) both land inside the node's own 13% band, so 'throughput does not rise at 64' holds either way - but the record cannot be reproduced by a reader, which is what it asks to be. Fix: plot the level's statistic (mean of three, with the two repeats as its band) and state the comparison against that same statistic.

The rejected-sample entry and the 13% band are mutually inconsistent, and the rejection has no criterion beyond the reading's own lowness. The note says the mis-dispatched c=64 attempt 'fired only 32 requests, so achieved concurrency was 32, not 64', i.e. by the node's own argument 26.13 req/min is a fourth sample of the c=32 population. The published band is computed as the ratio of the extremes of only the three samples that agree (36.45/32.01 = 13.9%); admitting the fourth, which the node itself assigns there, gives 36.45/26.13 = 40%. The band is the number the whole plateau argument is held to ('the 13% band is the upper bound the conclusion is held to'), and it is a max/min ratio rather than a spread of a distribution, over a sample of three. The classifying test is also circular as recorded: a run is excluded for reading low, but a genuine collapse above 32 would read low also - the discriminator the record gives is the dispatched count, which is a fact about the harness, not about the lane. This does not overturn the knee: the rise from c=16 (29.74) to c=32 survives on the mean either way (31.9 with 26.13 admitted), and no-rise at 64 survives too, so 32 stands as the lowest level beyond which throughput does not rise. Fix: publish the band as min/max over all samples the node attributes to the population, and keep the harness fact separate from the population it is claimed to describe.

justifications.durability: The number is specified well enough to be believed once and not yet well enough to be re-measured. On the credit side the record pins everything that defines the workload: endpoint URL and port, model id, served_by and max_model_len, the request body including temperature 0.0, max_tokens 700 and chat_template_kwargs {thinking: true, reasoning_effort: medium}, the 40-distinct-payload construction, the timeout deadline WITH its source constant named, and the starvation deadline with its rationale (8x solo latency - though the arithmetic is 9.3x against the recorded 6.42 s solo p50, a cosmetic slip). Every one of those is a fact a reader can check, and three of them I did check against live sources and they held. What is missing is the other half of reproducibility. The load generator is not committed and is not named by path, so re-running the sweep means rebuilding the harness from prose; the 40 payload identities are not listed; and the payload is rendered from LIVE templates over LIVE graph context, so 17,173 prompt tokens is a moving target - no digest of the rendered system or user prompt is recorded, so a re-run next week cannot be shown to be the same workload. That is the sharper edge of the node's own good lesson ('never carry a concurrency number across paths'): the corollary is that the number is only portable if what produced it is, and here the prompt is the thing that varies. Second, the plateau rests on one c=64 sample, so the honest statement is 'no rise detected at 64 on one sample' rather than a located knee; the record half-says this and then names 32 flatly. Third, the contamination check is declared but not performed: the record states that a concurrent worker would appear as exactly the measured spread, and there is a declared sibling node on the same served variant (n-the-compose-seat-is-measured-against-the-served-variant) whose live pointer is a stale 2026-09-18 entry, so nothing was loading the lane then; the c=1 distribution is in fact very tight (p50 6.42, p95 7.68, max 7.68 - one outlier-free wave) which is direct evidence the lane was quiet, and that evidence is not cited. The gap is small and the material is present in the file - it is the reasoning that was left out.
justifications.evidence: The record is honest, well-formed and the levels rederive exactly - and it publishes one figure that matches nothing in it. The rederivation I ran: every requests_per_min recomputes from n_requests/wall_s (16/105.33, 16/45.04, 16/35.87, 24/48.42, 32/52.67, 64/111.94 -> 9.11, 21.32, 26.76, 29.74, 36.45, 34.30), the repeat rows recompute likewise, and the figure's table agrees with the raw file row for row including the starvation and timeout columns. The rejected-sample entry is the best thing in the file: a first c=64 attempt that dispatched only 32 requests is recorded rather than deleted, with the reason and the achieved concurrency stated, and the record notes what publishing it would have wrongly concluded (a 40% collapse above 32 that does not exist). The instrument-limits paragraph is also unusually good practice - it names the login-node generator, states that no server-side gauge corroborated the client-side in-flight count (SSH key exchange refused, /metrics empty through the router, both of which I did not need to re-test because they are stated as limits rather than as findings), and pre-declares that a concurrent worker on this lane would present as exactly the spread measured. Docked eight for three things and they are all reporting rather than measurement. First, '0 of 184' (finding above): the level table is 168, the figure's rows are 232, performed-and-recorded is 264, and 184 is none of them - it appears in the commit body, the evidence anchor, the plan comment and the manifest, and the manifest contradicts itself in one field by printing both the per-level n list and the total. Second, 'raw per-level and per-request values' is asserted in three places and there are no per-request values; the level data satisfies the done-when, so this is an overstatement rather than a missing gate, but it is the sentence a reader follows to check the tail - and the tail is uncheckable, because c=64 alone has lat_p95 null while every other level has one. Third, the 13% band is a max/min ratio over the three agreeing samples, and the node's own rejected note assigns a fourth sample (26.13) to that same population, which would make the band 40%; the band is stated as 'the upper bound the conclusion is held to', so its aperture is load-bearing.
justifications.fit: The shape is the repository's: a figure under docs/figures/<topic>/ with a project-absolute src (/imas-codex/figures/sn-catalog-audit-instrument/local-lane-concurrency.svg, which is the path form the renderer needs), the raw values in a sibling file with the same stem, a landing section appended to the cumulative evidence archive, and a plan landing as an r-comment in the section that raised the question. The figure is a plot plus a table rather than a picture of a table, it carries the knee as a marked band rather than only in prose, and the comments on the path are what made the review tractable - endpoint, served_variant, criteria, rejected sample and platform note all sit in the machine-readable file, not only in the HTML. Binding the deadline to MODEL_TOKEN_LIMITS by name and then arguing why that constant is the wrong instrument at this knee (900 s cannot fire in range, so the 60 s starvation column is the earlier warning) is exactly the right relation between a measurement and the pipeline it informs - a measurement that adopted its own deadline would have been unfalsifiable. Docked four. The figure's subtitle carries the two-bases defect where it is most costly, since it is the sentence a reader quotes: it plots 36.45 and argues from 33.81 in the same breath. The curve then reads as a fall at the last point while the level's own three samples say flat, and the repeats are drawn as separate orange markers rather than as an uncertainty on the plotted point - defensible as a display choice, but it means the polyline and the prose describe different statistics and the file does not label which is which. The empty lat p95 column at c=64 and at the two repeats is carried faithfully from the raw file, and an unexplained dash in a table column is a small thing, but it is the column that would carry the tail and there is no note saying the value was not computed rather than lost.
justifications.goal_fidelity: VERDICT SOUND, and the question the plan needed answered is answered correctly. I verified the load's shape myself rather than accepting it: imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py:8689-8704 builds prompt_context as {**build_compose_context(), 'items': [item], neighbours, enum lists, 'review_scored_examples': ..., 'prior_reviews': []} and renders sn/review_names_system + sn/review_names_user over it, one name per request, at reasoning_effort from get_sn_review_reasoning_effort(). The node's payload construction ('render_prompt over build_compose_context()', 65,166 system chars, 17,173 prompt tokens, 694 generated, medium effort) is that same construction, so 'review-sized' is a fair designation rather than a hopeful one - and it is the designation the entire disagreement with the compose knee turns on. The environment claims are also independently checkable and I checked them: a GET /v1/models against http://98dci4-gpu-0003:18802/v1 returns {"id":"deepseek-v4.1-flash","owned_by":"sglang","max_model_len":512000}, confirming the served variant and the context figure the record asserts; and MODEL_TOKEN_LIMITS in imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py carries "timeout": 900 for both 'local' and 'hosted_vllm' exactly as cited, so the 900 s deadline is the pipeline's own and the starvation column is the right substitute for it. The knee meets the done-when's letter: throughput rises at every sampled level through 32 (9.11, 21.32, 26.76, 29.74, 36.45) and does not rise at 64 (34.30), with starvation appearing there (43 of 64 past 60 s), so 32 is the lowest level beyond which throughput does not rise. The mechanism offered for the disagreement with the compose probe - generated tokens per request, ~18.5k decode-bound against ~694 prompt-dominated - is the correct discriminator and is consistent with the pre-existing compose measurement. Docked four. The c=32 level point is the maximum of its three samples while the prose argues from their mean, so the figure overstates the plateau's fall by 7 points of relative difference. The single c=64 sample is the level the knee is named against and it was run once while c=32 was run three times, an asymmetry on exactly the comparison that carries the conclusion. And the knee is named at a grid point (32) without a level between 16 and 32 or between 32 and 64, so the record should say the knee is 32 ON THIS GRID - the plan's own posture is to avoid encoding a number neither side re-measured, and 32 is a sampled level, not a located knee.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 9b4bd7bc8946162acca4592a444ee495f15b5338 8beb1c4ee is exactly four paths and every one is inside a declared write path: docs/figures/sn-catalog-audit-instrument/local-lane-concurrency.svg, docs/figures/sn-catalog-audit-instrument/local-lane-concurrency-raw.json (inside the declared directory docs/figures/sn-catalog-audit-instrument), docs/evidence/archive/sn-catalog-audit-instrument-landed.html and docs/plans/sn-catalog-audit-instrument.html. 220 insertions, no deletions, four files. The plan edit is a single worker-owned r-comment with data-section="s4", and it explicitly declines to close the node: 'This node measures and records; setting the instrument's default from it, and the merged-result verification, belong elsewhere' - which is the coordinator's call to make, not the worker's, and the worker left it there. No plan-version or plan-modified meta line is touched, so this edit cannot conflict with any other worker's. The commit has a conventional subject AND a substantive body stating what changed and why. A case-insensitive scan of the message for co-authored-by / generated with / claude / copilot returns zero hits. data-who="reckon-ship-worker" matches the convention already used five times in this plan. A label scan over the two new figure files returns one hit, on line 1 of the SVG (its root element's width/height/viewBox attributes) - no plan, phase, stage, sprint or ticket label appears in any visible text of the figure or anywhere in the raw record. No branch was created, nothing was pushed, and the shared index was not touched.
